html:
The first farming culture of Taiwan, found on the island's coasts and on the Penghu Islands from about 4000 to 3000 BCE. The map shows it in 3000 BCE.

Its people made pottery decorated with cord marks, used polished stone tools, fished and gathered shellfish, and probably grew some crops. Most scholars think they came across the Taiwan Strait from the coast of Fujian in mainland China.

The Dapenkeng people are widely seen as ancestors of Taiwan's indigenous peoples and so of the Austronesians. From Taiwan their descendants later sailed south, reaching the Philippines by about 2200 BCE and in time settling islands from Madagascar to Easter Island. That makes this small coastal culture the starting point of one of the largest migrations in human history.
